title: Curved circles from coins: the random split law and the isotropic law
claim: Coins bend circles. (1) In Z^2 with one diagonal per unit square (NE with probability p independently, NW otherwise), the graph distance between u <= w is exactly (w_x - u_x) + (w_y - u_y) minus the longest strictly increasing chain of NE squares in the box [u, w] (NW squares in the other quadrants). (2) Conditional on Seppalainen's law of large numbers (Ann. Appl. Probab. 7 (1997), Theorem 1, cited): this distance divided by n converges a.s. to c_p(z) = |z_x| + |z_y| - g_q(|z_x|, |z_y|), g_q(s, t) = (2 sqrt(q s t) - q (s + t))/(1 - q) for q s <= t <= s/q and min(s, t) otherwise, q = p in the first and third quadrants and 1 - p in the others; and the bond distance of the dual law (the square law with each four-place knot split into two three-place knots by the coin) divided by n converges in probability to 2 c_p(z). So the circle is a square with elliptic corners (|x| + |y| - (1 - q))^2 = 4 q |x||y|, circular for p = 1/2, with pi = 2 + 6/sqrt(5) - 4 sqrt(2) int_{1/sqrt 2}^{sqrt 2} u^2 (1 + u^4)^(-3/2) du = 3.44120 at p = 1/2 and the hexagon (pi = 3) at p = 0 or 1. (3) Conditional on Kingman's subadditive ergodic theorem and the positive Delaunay time constant (Vahidi-Asl-Wierman): the parity law on the Voronoi tessellation of a planar Poisson process (all knots three-place) has an exactly round circle.
failure_conditions: An environment and a pair u <= w whose breadth-first distance differs from (w_x - u_x) + (w_y - u_y) minus the longest strictly increasing chain of NE squares in the box.
A direction z in which bond distance divided by n stays away from 2 c_p(z) at growing n.
A direction in which the Voronoi law's bond distance per unit distance converges to a different constant.
foundation_claim_scope: The random split law for every p in [0, 1] (items 1-2); the Poisson-Voronoi law in the plane (item 3).

validation.independence: Written by Claude in one session at the repository owner's request on 2026-11-07.
validation.status: prose proofs of Theorems 1-3 and 5 and Corollary 4, conditional on cited published theorems; check.py (21 s) verifies the exact formula on 36,963 targets, the cited constants on 3000 x 3000 samples, exact least cycles within 2d + 1 .. 2d + 8 with shrinking deviation from 2 c_p, the shape equations, pi two ways, and Voronoi adjacent pairs, with four rejected controls; no human or external review
validation.novelty: known-overlap-found: strictly increasing chains in Bernoulli lattices (Seppalainen 1997), first-passage percolation on Voronoi and Delaunay graphs is round (Vahidi-Asl and Wierman 1990, 1992); the delta is the exact distance formula for Z^2 with random diagonals, the reduction of bond distance to it with two disjoint near-geodesics, the circular corners at p = 1/2 and the reading for parity laws.
